newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH optimistic for second half earnings.
newsitem.headline: CHH optimistic for second half earnings.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd said on Thursday it was optimistic the improvement in operating earnings seen in the second quarter would continue into the second half.
Second quarter earnings were 11 percent ahead of the first quarter, reflecting a significant improvement in operating performance across its businesses.
"The company is optimistic that the low point in the current cycle for most of its products has been passed, Chief Executive John Faraci said.

"While the business environment in major markets remains highly competitive, the company believes that the modest improvement in trading conditions will continue through to the end of the financial year," he said.
CHH earlier reported a net profit after tax of NZ$118 million in the six months to September, down from $271 million a year earlier.
Earnings before interest and tax were up 46 percent over the first quarter.
"In most cases, improvements were the results of productivity, margin improvement and cost reduction," Chief Executive John Faraci said.
"While the result for the six months to September 30 is down on the same period in 1995, the 1995 result reflected the peak of the pulp and paper price cycle," he said.
Since the start of the financial year the Northern Europe delivered price of softwood pulp had risen from about US$500 per tonne to $550 by the end of September.
The acquisition of Forward Products in August 1996 enabled CHH to consolidate its position and become a major participant in the Australian softwood products markets, Faraci said.
Cost reduction remained a key focus for management and it was anticipated that savings in logistics and procurement alone would be NZ$25 million in the current year, rising to $50 million in 1997/8.

"The fundamentals for the medium term remain sound for all businesses and the company will continue to invest in its existing businesses and pursue cost reduction opportunities to ensure that businesses remain competitive," Faraci said.
"The company remains committed to expanding the operating base of its core businesses, both in New Zealand and overseas," Faraci said.
